# Codex CLI Permissions — Spec

## Purpose

Record the current Codex CLI sandbox, approval, network, and Unix-socket
surfaces. Sandboxing defines what commands can do; approval policy
independently defines whether Codex may ask before attempting an action.

## Stable command surface

The current CLI exposes three sandbox modes:

- `read-only`
- `workspace-write`
- `danger-full-access`

Select the mode with `--sandbox` / `-s`. Disable approval prompts with
`--ask-for-approval never` / `-a never`; this does not disable the sandbox.
`--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` removes both controls.

The sandbox and approval controls can be combined explicitly:

```bash
codex --sandbox workspace-write --ask-for-approval never
```

`codex exec --full-auto` is deprecated compatibility syntax. New automation
uses explicit sandbox and approval flags. `codex exec --ignore-user-config`
prevents ambient `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml` from entering a controlled
non-interactive run; `--ignore-rules` separately skips user and project
execpolicy rules.

## Workspace boundary

`workspace-write` permits reads and command execution while restricting writes
to the active workspace and configured writable roots. Protected paths remain
read-only within writable roots, including `.git`, `.agents`, and `.codex`.
Additional writable directories require explicit `--add-dir` arguments.

In a linked Git worktree, `.git` is a pointer file. The default
`workspace-write` policy also protects the Git directory to which it points.
Git commands that update the worktree index or refs can therefore encounter a
write denial. An added directory is a write grant, not a read-only mount. The
installed 0.157.1 CLI exposes `--sandbox workspace-write`,
`--ask-for-approval never`, `--add-dir`, and `--strict-config`.

Network access is off by default in `workspace-write`. Enabling constrained
networking is a separate configuration action; enabling a network-policy
feature does not itself grant network access.

## Unix-socket boundary

Current configuration supports allowlist-first Unix-socket policy under:

```toml
[permissions.workspace.network.unix_sockets]
"/absolute/path/to/assigned.sock" = "allow"
```

`dangerously_allow_all_unix_sockets` defaults to `false`. The Unix-socket
allowlist is separate from
filesystem write grants and ordinary outbound network settings.

The `codex sandbox` helper exposes lower-level controls:

- `--sandbox-state-json <JSON>` consumes sandbox state generated by the Codex
  runtime.
- `--sandbox-state-disable-network` removes direct network access from supplied
  state.
- repeatable `--allow-unix-socket <PATH>` allows AF_UNIX access rooted at the
  named path.
- `--permission-profile <NAME>` resolves a named permission profile from the
  active configuration stack.

The helper accepts sandbox state generated by the Codex runtime. A manually
constructed state has not been verified as equivalent to the state used by an
interactive Codex session.

## Profiles

`--profile <NAME>` layers a named configuration file on top of base config.
Profile names are user-defined; the CLI does not define `safe`, `default`,
`full-auto`, or `danger` as a standard four-profile model. A profile name
alone does not specify its filesystem permissions.

Fine-grained permission profiles are a separate beta surface and do not compose
with the older `sandbox_mode` / `[sandbox_workspace_write]` settings. Passing
`--sandbox`, or loading any config layer that sets `sandbox_mode`, selects the
older sandbox model instead of `default_permissions`. A custom permission
profile is selected without `--sandbox`; approval policy remains a separate
control.

The profile filesystem map accepts `read`, `write`, and `deny` entries. Its
special roots include `:workspace_roots` and `:tmpdir`; specific entries can
override broader grants. The profile's Unix-socket map allows individual
absolute socket paths. The installed CLI exposes
`codex sandbox --permission-profile <name>` and repeatable
`--allow-unix-socket <path>` for a local command probe. Whether a custom
profile can grant writes to the protected linked-worktree Git directory in
this installed build has not been exercised.

Permission profiles govern local sandboxed command execution. Connectors, MCP
servers, browser and computer-use surfaces have separate controls.

## Gaps / Unknowns

- Filesystem, network, and Unix-socket behavior of a custom permission profile
  has not been exercised against the installed CLI on each supported OS.
